title: Atomic HINs: Entity-Attribute Duality for Heterogeneous Graph Modeling
claim: The same source data can be organized into many different schemas, and existing fixed designs are only some heuristic choices among alternatives.
layout: 4 panels, left-to-right, schema diagrams with UML-style boxes and captions below
description: Four schema diagrams in a row, each drawn as UML-like boxes joined by gray lines. Panel (a), 'Original data', shows one gray Movie table with attributes director, actor, keyword, country, content rating and language. Panel (b), 'IMDb (Fu et al., 2020)', shows a peach Movie box keeping keyword, country, content rating and language. It links to peach Actor and Director boxes that each hold a keyword attribute. Panel (c), 'IMDb (Lv et al., 2021)', shows a light-gray Movie box with Keyword, Actor and Director boxes branching off it. Actor and Director each hold a keyword attribute. Panel (d), 'Alternative schema', shows a teal Movie box with Country and Language boxes that each hold a director attribute. Color separates the variants. The eye starts at the single table on the left and then follows the branching schemas to the right.
caption: Illustration of multiple heterogeneous schemas derived from the same IMDb source table.
abstract: Heterogeneous Information Networks (HINs) provide a powerful framework for modeling multi-typed entities and relations, typically defined under a fixed schema. Yet, most research assumes this structure is given, overlooking the fact that alternative designs can emphasize different aspects of the data and substantially influence downstream performance. As a theoretical foundation for such designs, we introduce the principle of entity-attribute duality: attributes can be atomized as entities with their associated relations, while entities can, in turn, serve as attributes of others. This principle motivates atomic HIN, a canonical representation that makes all modeling choices explicit and achieves maximal expressiveness. Building on this foundation, we propose a systematic framework for task-specific schema refinement. Within this framework, we demonstrate that widely used benchmarks correspond to heuristic refinements of the atomic HIN—often far from optimal. Across eight datasets, refinement alone enables a simplified Relational GCN (sRGCN) to achieve state-of-the-art performance on node- and link-level tasks, with further gains from advanced HGNNs. These results highlight schema design as a key dimension in heterogeneous graph modeling. By releasing the atomic HINs, searched schemas, and refinement framework, we enable principled benchmarking and open the way for future work on schema-aware learning, automated structure discovery, and next-generation HGNNs. Our code is available at: https://github.com/ntuidssplab/AtomHIN.
